title: Customer Signal Tally — Mini Probes & Pragmatic Fixes (quickcut)
high_level_summary: Quick tally of customer feedback from Dec '25 — Jan '26 focused on operational friction and small-scope feature asks. Goal: surface 6 low-effort, high-impact probes + 3 medium-effort experiments for engineering/product to triage. This is a field-first, engineering-aware synthesis — heavy on explicit next steps and owners.
body:
Context and method:
- Source window: Dec 01 2025 — Jan 12 2026. Inputs: support tickets, CSM call notes (10 customers), community threads, 3 enterprise onboarding projects.
- Tally approach: tag each ask by (a) customer frequency, (b) user-visible impact, (c) engineering effort estimate (quick/mid/heavy).
- Intent: prioritize things that unblock adoption or reduce repeated operational toil. Not a product roadmap doc; this is a tactical playbook for the next 6 sprints.

Observed themes (short):
1) Endpoint/control surface friction (30 mentions) — customers want clearer route-level limits, per-route token caps, and easier rollbacks for model rollouts.
2) Latency variability and tail spikes (25 mentions) — most acute for chat/streaming with long contexts; enterprise customers call out tail p99s that break UX.
3) Cost surprises from batching/caching (18 mentions) — teams saw higher-than-expected token usage due to prefix expansion and hidden retries.
4) Quantization artifacts & hallucination variance (14 mentions) — customers using quantized variants report occasional output drift relative to full-precision model.
5) Observability gaps (22 mentions) — need per-request model variant attribution, KV cache hit rates, and clearer token cost breakdowns per route.
6) Private deploy onboarding snags (10 mentions) — network/TLS cert provisioning and KMS mapping slow initial seat-up.

Representative customer vignettes (anonymized):
- "RetailBot" (mid-market PLG): kept increasing timeout to avoid mid-response failures; p99 spikes meant chat UI showed disconnected state — wants per-route fallback to smaller model instead of retry.
- "SecureForms" (enterprise): worried about quantized embedding drift for semantic search; wants an automated eval harness between model variants.
- "EdgeAssist" (startup): high token bill due to unseen prefix replication from client-side retries; asks for per-request trace that shows batch/duplication contribution to billed tokens.

Low-effort quick wins (<= 2 dev-days each) [6 items]:
- QW1: Add a per-route token cap UI field (default unset) and server-side enforcement. Quick UX + backend flag. Owner: Jonah.
- QW2: Expose `x-cache-hit` header and a simple histogram in Console for KV cache hits (last 24h). Owner: Marta.
- QW3: Add a transparent "cost delta" line on Console deploy pages that shows estimated tokens saved by enabling prefix caching. Owner: CSM -> eng frontline.
- QW4: Expose model-variant label in request tracing (so users can see 'fallback-quant' vs 'primary'). Very small telemetry change. Owner: Ibrahim.
- QW5: Default a safety rollback policy on new rollouts (canary -> auto-rollback if error rate > X%). Configurable toggle. Owner: Product ops.
- QW6: Small docs sprint: "How to avoid duplicate token billing from retries" one-pager + sample client snippet. Owner: Priya.

Medium-effort experiments (1–3 sprints) [3 items]:
- ME1: Probe automatic fallback routing by latency bands: route requests with p90 < threshold to primary, else to a cheaper quantized variant with a warmed prefix cache. Deliverables: A/B experiment, metrics dashboard (latency/cost/quality). Owner: serving-runtime + optimize. Hypothesis: 20–30% cost reduction on bursty routes with <2% qual regression.
- ME2: Small quantized-vs-fp evaluation harness: nightly automated eval on 5 customer prompt-sets (anonymized) with regression alerting. Deliverables: CI job + Slack alerting + Console flag to opt into model-variant comparisons. Owner: applied-ml + product.
- ME3: Per-route request trace UI: allow customers to unroll a single request and see batching, retries, model selection, and billed tokens. This is heavier (storage/UX) but high value for enterprise billing disputes. Owner: observability.

Open questions & unknowns (for discussion):
- What is the SLA/expectation on model-variant labels being 'authoritative' vs 'best-effort'? Ops cost if we require 100% accuracy.
- How many customers would enable automated fallback to quantized variant if we show a live quality delta? Risk: hidden regressions.
- Are there privacy/compliance blockers for exposing per-request traces for private deployments? (KMS/PII concerns)

Short-run triage recommendations (next two weeks):
- Triage meeting with eng-serving-runtime + observability + product to commit owners for QW1–QW4.
- Kickoff ME1 A/B experiment design doc (1-pager) and sample traffic slice.
- Publish the docs one-pager (QW6) and a short email to cohort of 10 largest affected customers.

Suggested immediate tickets to create (CSR->ENG template):
- CS-1409: Add per-route token cap enforcement + UI (ref: QW1).
- CS-1410: Expose x-cache-hit header + simple Console histogram (ref: QW2).
- CS-1411: Model-variant label in tracer payload (ref: QW4).

Measurement plan (how we'll know success):
- Quick-wins: adoption metrics (how many routes set per-route caps; cache-histogram views) and reduction in related support tickets over 30 days.
- ME1: A/B metric: cost per 1k requests and quality regression rate (auto-eval on sample prompt-set). Target: >=15% cost down without >2% quality loss.

Notes to self / CSM playbook snippets (keep handy):
- When a customer reports tail p99s, ask for a sample trace and recommend temporary per-route caps and canary fallback to smaller model.
- For embedding drift concerns, suggest enabling nightly eval harness and share example diff reports.

Next steps and owners (summary):
- Week 0–1: Create tickets CS-1409..1411. Owners assigned above.
- Week 1–2: Run docs/email to cohort + small UX copy changes.
- Week 2–6: ME1 experiment design & rollout.

Unresolved / parking lot (for product forum):
- Consider per-customer default quantization profiles (auto-recommend) — long lead time.
- Investigate per-request token re-attribution for third-party retry libraries — depends on SDK changes.

Appendix (raw counts):
- Endpoint/control surface friction: 30 mentions
- Latency variability / p99 spikes: 25 mentions
- Observability gaps: 22 mentions
- Cost/billing surprises: 18 mentions
- Quantization drift concerns: 14 mentions
- Private deploy onboarding snags: 10 mentions

End of quickcut. This is intentionally terse — use it as a field-run ticket feeder. If useful, I can expand into a full 1-pager with mockups for QW1 and ME1.
high_priority_actions: Create tickets CS-1409, CS-1410, CS-1411 and assign owners
Schedule triage with serving-runtime + observability + product
Publish docs one-pager and notify top-10 affected customers
microproposals: Docs: avoid duplicate billing from retries
Nightly quantized-vs-fp automated evals for customer prompt-sets
customer_vignettes: RetailBot: p99 spikes break chat UI; wants model fallback not retry
SecureForms: embedding drift vs quantized variant; asks for automated evals
EdgeAssist: token bill spike from client retries; wants per-request billing trace
notes_for_engineering: Keep variant labels light-weight (header + minimal telemetry)
Cache-hit header should be boolean + sample ratio header
Per-route caps should default to unset to avoid accidental throttles
conclusion: There are multiple small, high-leverage fixes we can ship quickly to reduce repeat support load and improve adoption. Focus first on per-route limits, lightweight telemetry (cache hits + variant labels), and a short docs push. Then run 1 medium experiment (fallback-by-latency) to measure cost/quality tradeoffs.
